text: This chunk discusses the causes, transmission, and mechanisms of German measles (Rubella). It explains that the disease is caused by the Rubella virus, which belongs to the Togaviridae family. The virus is found in the mucus, saliva, and phlegm of infected individuals and can be easily destroyed by various disinfectants and environmental conditions. Transmission occurs through respiratory droplets and contact with contaminated surfaces. The virus enters the body through the respiratory system, spreads to the bloodstream, and affects lymph nodes, liver, and spleen. The incubation period is typically 12-24 days, and the infectious period is from 5 days before to 6 days after the rash appears. The disease often spreads in schools, factories, and workplaces, particularly from January to April.
